description: Return every city ranked in the top 10, including all cities tied with the 10th, so the result may have more than 10 rows.

b.request: For each city in the address table (grouped by city_id), show city_id, the number of addresses, that count divided by the average addresses per city, and its share of all addresses (count divided by total addresses), unrounded, and return all cities whose share ranks in the top 10 when ordered from highest to lowest, including every city tied with the 10th-ranked share, so the result may have more than 10 rows
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id), s AS (SELECT city_id, address_count, address_count * 1.0 / AVG(address_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg, address_count * 1.0 / SUM(address_count) OVER () AS share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY address_count * 1.0 / SUM(address_count) OVER () DESC) AS rnk FROM c) SELECT city_id, address_count, ratio_to_avg, share FROM s WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC, city_id

c.request: For each city in the address table, show its city ID, how many addresses it has, that count relative to the average number of addresses per city, and its share of all addresses. Which are the top 10 cities by that share, highest first? Don't round anything. Return every city ranked in the top 10, including all cities tied with the 10th, so the result may have more than 10 rows.
c.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id), s AS (SELECT city_id, address_count, address_count * 1.0 / (SELECT AVG(address_count * 1.0) FROM c) AS relative_to_avg, address_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(address_count) FROM c) AS share FROM c), r AS (SELECT s.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM s) SELECT city_id, address_count, relative_to_avg, share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC, city_id

a.request: For each `city_id` in the address table, show the city ID, its number of addresses, that count divided by the average number of addresses per city, and that count as a share of all addresses (count divided by the total number of addresses). Rank cities by that share from highest to lowest and return every city ranked in the top 10, including all cities tied with the 10th, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id), s AS (SELECT c.*, CAST(c.address_count AS REAL) / (SELECT AVG(address_count) FROM c) AS ratio_to_avg, CAST(c.address_count AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM address) AS share FROM c), r AS (SELECT s.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM s) SELECT city_id, address_count, ratio_to_avg, share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC, city_id
